examples.why: 0 using directives versus 53 in ILSpy, so all 3,970 type references are fully qualified; plus 857 unnecessary global:: prefixes (735 in this type alone).
examples.fix: Emit the using set for the referenced namespaces, prefer the shortest unambiguous name (System.Int32 -> int, System.Type -> Type), and drop global:: when there is no ambiguity. When substituting the __cil_ref_/__cil_type_ aliases, also map CLI element types (uint8[] -> byte[]); those names currently appear only inside the alias comments, never in code.
examples.risk: none - the only work is the ambiguity check when two namespaces hold the same simple name.

examples.why: CR and LF are printed as \u000D/\u000A: 1,004 pairs over 139 lines (1,730 escapes in this type, 258 in JObjectTests, 20 in ExceptionHandlingTests, 0 in JPathParseTests). The printer is otherwise correct - the only other escapes are \u0000 (1, a genuine NUL) and \\u003c (1, matching ILSpy). Because this is a serializer test suite, expected-JSON literals are the core payload and they are unreadable.
examples.fix: Use the short escapes \r \n \t \0 \" \\ and fall back to \uXXXX only for other control characters.
examples.risk: none - purely lexical, provable with a printer round-trip test.

notes: Line ratios: JsonSerializerTest 2.79, JObjectTests 3.27, JPathParseTests 3.21, ExceptionHandlingTests 5.16 (slice 3.19). The slice is NUnit test code with heavy compiler machinery, which is why it is far worse than a plain business-logic type would be.

Two root causes explain most of the excess: opaque token-named calls (2,978 sites, which forces 8,203 vN temporaries) and compiler machinery printed literally (112 synthetic nested types, plus 74 of the 122 fallbacks caused by display-class allocation).

The string printer is NOT escaping every character: the whole slice contains 1,004 \u000D, 1,004 \u000A, one \u0000 (a genuine NUL in JSON) and one \\u003c (which matches ILSpy). The defect is exactly the CR/LF short escapes, on 139 lines.

The same token is sometimes resolved (v1.Add, v15.TryGetValue, Newtonsoft.Json.Linq.JsonPath.QueryFilter in a cast) and sometimes not (__cil_callvirt_0A00092A). JPathParseTests resolves 0 member calls against 496 helper calls, so its output has no named statement at all.

Deliberately kept lowered and NOT counted as defects: lambdas/closures (208 sites), dynamic (1 site), foreach (5 sites). Their identifier and comment cost is still reported because renaming and moving comments behind --details requires none of the missing analysis.
No occurrence of ??, ?. or switch in either output, so those categories have no instances in this slice.
Every claim was read from the paired files and index.json in this directory; no decompiler was re-run and no input code was executed.
